title: Birthday Directory Sample
description: A directory-shaped fixture for testing whether mobile feed views work better than snap or story views for peer records.

sections.title: January
sections.body: Ada Lovelace, Zora Neale Hurston, and Martin Luther King Jr. make January a useful test month for dense biographical cards.

sections.title: February
sections.body: Frederick Douglass, Rosa Parks, and Toni Morrison create a second set of records with short summaries and easy comparison.

sections.title: March
sections.body: Albert Einstein, Ruth Bader Ginsburg, and Cesar Chavez are grouped as another peer set rather than a narrative sequence.

sections.title: April
sections.body: Maya Angelou, Leonardo da Vinci, and Ella Fitzgerald help test how a feed handles varied domains and longer names.

sections.title: May
sections.body: Audrey Hepburn, Malcolm X, and Rachel Carson close the sample with enough items to make the card-feed rhythm obvious.

assets.alt: Four presentation surfaces derived from one Capsule data model.

cards.title: Birthday Directory
cards.body: A record set wants browsing, not a forced story.

cards.title: Peer items
cards.body: Each month is a comparable card, so feed should beat snap for quick scanning.

cards.title: Scan first
cards.body: The reader should see multiple options and choose where to slow down.

cards.title: Compare easily
cards.body: Repeated card structure makes names, months, and notes easy to compare.

cards.title: Feed wins
cards.body: Directory content is the natural home for the mobile feed style.
